questions.q: Which four metrics commonly dominate a service/support dashboard?
options: Pipeline value, win rate, quota, forecast category
Case volume, case age, response/resolution time, customer satisfaction
Lead source, campaign ROI, conversion rate, cost per lead
Account rating, territory, industry, employee count
questions.explain: Support dashboards center on volume, age, speed (response/resolution time), and quality (satisfaction) — the sales-specific metrics like win rate and quota belong to pipeline reporting instead.

questions.q: In a Cases report grouped by Status with Priority as a second grouping, what question does that Matrix format answer that a single grouping by Status alone can't?
options: The average deal size in the pipeline
How many cases of each priority level are sitting in each status, such as how many urgent cases are open
Which report folder the cases are stored in
The total number of custom report types in the org
questions.explain: Adding Priority as a second grouping breaks volume down by urgency as well as status, turning a flat count into a far more actionable view of what needs attention first.

questions.q: Why does case age matter on top of a simple open-case volume count?
options: Case age replaces the need for a Status field entirely
A case open for three weeks looks identical to one opened an hour ago on a pure volume report, hiding a real problem
Case age is only relevant for closed cases
Case age determines a case's report type automatically
questions.explain: Volume alone doesn't distinguish how long a case has been sitting. Case age is the field that surfaces cases that are stuck, the support equivalent of a stalled opportunity.

questions.q: What does reporting on time-to-first-response and time-to-resolution actually accomplish?
options: It removes the need for case prioritization
It turns a vague sense of "are we fast enough" into measurable numbers, including the percentage breaching target
It automatically closes cases that take too long
It converts Cases into Opportunities for sales follow-up
questions.explain: Reporting average response and resolution times, plus the percentage breaching whatever target or SLA applies, gives leadership concrete numbers instead of a general impression of speed.

questions.q: Case volume on a dashboard is trending down, which looks like good news. What should you check before concluding support performance has genuinely improved?
options: Whether the dashboard's folder is shared correctly
Case age and resolution time — volume alone doesn't show whether remaining or past cases are being resolved well or just going stale
Whether the report type is custom or standard
Nothing further is needed; lower volume always means better performance
questions.explain: Falling volume could mean genuinely faster resolution, or it could mean cases are sitting unresolved and simply not being logged as new. Age and resolution-time metrics are needed to tell the difference.
